The Committee’s decision to hold the policy rate while highlighting “lags” is consistent with New Keynesian/DSGE practice used at the Fed (e.g., Woodford; Lubik and Schorfheide 2004), where output and inflation respond to policy with delays. The statement that tighter financial and credit conditions will weigh on activity accords with the credit channel and financial accelerator literature (Bernanke and Gertler; agency-cost mechanisms), implying downside growth risks beyond the standard interest-rate channel. Emphasis on the 2 percent inflation objective and expectations is aligned with the Phillips curve framework and sticky-information dynamics (Mankiw and Reis 2002), suggesting inflation persistence and a rationale for a still-restrictive stance. Ongoing balance sheet reduction and SOMA directives that influence long-term rates and the yield curve (Cochrane and Piazzesi) reinforce tight financial conditions even without additional hikes. Acknowledging low unemployment but moderating job gains fits a cautious, data-dependent approach, mindful of real-time measurement uncertainty (Orphanides 2001). Overall tone: cautiously restrictive with balanced risks, slightly negative for near-term growth.
